# Original Schema binding observations

The pinned original TypeScript SHA256 is
`a6647b515659cf439b701fa9f9574c9c310ce3872d26a13a81e9fa4d02ba10ad`.
`schema-binding-patterns-provenance.json` records exact source, offsets and hashes
for five lexical declarations and23 parameter patterns. The other original
plain-array for-of binding is already covered by the existing loop qualification.

The reference contains those original patterns with only ES2022 type erasure,
inside explicit projection wrappers. The Mithril fixture admits the corresponding
patterns and emits native destructuring through both actual CLI targets. Each
target runs117 finite observations: defaults including undefined/null, renaming,
ordered getters, throwing values, and original initializer argument/path shapes.
`Schema.resolve` is an explicit observation grant, not an actual Schema runtime
substitute. Parameters are projected in observation wrappers, not their complete
original callback bodies; original callback arity is not claimed by these wrappers.

The separate independent native mechanics oracle has30 paired groups per target/profile (standalone and native ESM):
iterator step/close/rest/nesting, object proxy/computed/symbol/inherited keys,
TDZ/shadowing/mutation, inferred names, native parameter length/arguments/this,
async/generator source scopes and class/object/local/hoisted signatures. Tests
compare application exceptions by identity and built-in exception classes;
engine diagnostic text can include compiler-owned variable names.

This is finite binding qualification under Node. Full Schema/default export,
actual browser/native/Q9 and complete Harness API/plugin equivalence remain
separate gates. The full source-authoring probe now reaches the `0.01` literal in
percent(); Mithril form admission currently refuses that decimal source value.
Neither individual projections nor an authored document proves a complete port.
